{{short description|Result in the presentation theory of mathematical groups}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Freiheitssatz''' ([[German language|German]]: "freedom/independence theorem": ''[[wikt:Freiheit|Freiheit]]'' + ''[[wikt:Satz|Satz]]'') is a result in the [[Presentation of a group|presentation theory]] of [[group (mathematics)|groups]], stating that certain subgroups of a [[one-relator group]] are [[free group]]s.

==Statement==
Consider a group presentation
:<math>G = \langle x_{1}, \dots, x_{n} | r = 1 \rangle</math>
given by {{mvar|n}} generators {{math|''x''<sub>''i''</sub>}} and a single [[Cyclically reduced word|cyclically reduced]] relator {{mvar|r}}. If {{math|''x''<sub>1</sub>}} appears in {{mvar|r}}, then (according to the freiheitssatz) the [[subgroup]] of {{mvar|G}} generated by {{math|''x''<sub>2</sub>, ..., ''x''<sub>''n''</sub>}} is a [[free group]], freely generated by {{math|''x''<sub>2</sub>, ..., ''x''<sub>''n''</sub>}}. In other words, the only relations involving {{math|''x''<sub>2</sub>, ..., ''x''<sub>''n''</sub>}} are the trivial ones.

==History==
The result was proposed by the [[Germany|German]] [[mathematician]] [[Max Dehn]] and proved by his student, [[Wilhelm Magnus]], in his doctoral thesis.<ref> {{cite journal
|     last = Magnus
|    first = Wilhelm
|author-link= Wilhelm Magnus
|    title = Über diskontinuierliche Gruppen mit einer definierenden Relation. (Der Freiheitssatz)
|  journal = J. Reine Angew. Math.
|   volume = 163
|     year = 1930
|    pages = 141&ndash;165
}}</ref> Although Dehn expected Magnus to find a [[topology|topological]] proof,<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Stillwell | first = John | author-link = John Stillwell
 | editor-last = James | editor-first = I. M.
 | contribution = Max Dehn
 | isbn = 0-444-82375-1
 | mr = 1674906
 | pages = 965–978
 | publisher = North-Holland, Amsterdam
 | title = History of topology
 | year = 1999}} See in particular [https://books.google.com/books?id=7iRijkz0rrUC&pg=PA973 p.&nbsp;973].</ref> Magnus instead found a proof based on [[mathematical induction]]<ref name="ls"/> and [[amalgamated product]]s of groups.<ref name="eom"/> Different induction-based proofs were given later by {{harvtxt|Lyndon|1972}} and {{harvtxt|Weinbaum|1972}}.<ref name="ls">{{cite book
 | last1 = Lyndon | first1 = Roger C. | author1-link = Roger Lyndon

 | year = 2001}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal

==Significance==
The Freiheitssatz has become "the cornerstone of one-relator group theory", and motivated the development of the theory of [[amalgamated product]]s. It also provides an analogue, in non-commutative group theory, of certain results on [[vector space]]s and other commutative groups.<ref name="eom">{{springer|author=V.A. Roman'kov|id=f/f120170|title=Freiheitssatz}}</ref>
